Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan have agreed to activate the collective defense clause of their Makkah Alliance, according to a joint statement published by Pakistan's Foreign Ministry after an emergency meeting in Riyadh.

The alliance's Strategic Political and Defence Committee decided to move immediately to practical implementation, with Ankara and Islamabad committing to provide previously agreed forces and military capabilities and deploy them rapidly in the kingdom. No troop numbers or timeline were disclosed, and the deployment is subject to each country's national laws.

The decision comes amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Ansar Allah, whose strikes on Saudi territory prompted Riyadh to call the meeting. Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman said the alliance was triggered in response to the attacks and those behind them.

🎙 Iranian envoys to Thailand, Vatican and South Africa report to Araghchi

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The ambassadors of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Thailand, the Vatican, and South Africa have met with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to discuss the latest status of relations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and their respective countries of assignment.

Nasseredin Heidari, the Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Thailand, met on Monday with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi to discuss the latest state of relations between Tehran and Bangkok and future prospects.
​
Highlighting Thailand’s position in Southeast Asia and ASEAN, Araghchi emphasized strengthening relations between Tehran and Bangkok—particularly in the economic and trade sectors—and activating existing potential in the political, economic, and parliamentary arenas.
​
Furthermore, while reviewing various aspects of Iran-Thailand relations, the two sides examined ways to more effectively utilize mutual potential and create new avenues for expanding bilateral ties.
​
Meeting between Ambassador of Islamic Republic of Iran to Vatican and Foreign Minister
​
Additionally, Mohammad-Hossein Mokhtari, the Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the Vatican, met and held talks with the Foreign Minister today.
​
During the meeting, the Iranian Ambassador to the Vatican presented a report on the mission's latest activities and outlined upcoming plans to expand and enhance cooperation between Iran and the Vatican.
​
During this meeting, the latest status of bilateral relations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Vatican, the potential inherent in shared religious values, and the role of interfaith dialogue in expanding and deepening ties between the two sides were also discussed and reviewed.
​
Meeting between Ambassador of Islamic Republic of Iran to South Africa and Minister of Foreign Affairs
​
Mansour Shakib-Mehr, the Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to South Africa, also met with the Foreign Minister to discuss the current state of relations between Tehran and Pretoria and future prospects.
​
During the meeting, the Foreign Minister highlighted South Africa's status and role within the African continent and in international organizations such as BRICS, emphasizing the importance of strengthening ties between Tehran and Pretoria.
​
Araghchi also commended the initiatives undertaken by the missions of the Islamic Republic of Iran—particularly the mission in South Africa—in the realm of media and digital diplomacy, as well as the efforts made during the forty-day war, which had a significant impact and resonance among global public opinion.

Macronomics: The Fire Sale

Nine years ago, Emmanuel Macron promised to turn France into Europe’s pro-business engine. 

Finance Minister Roland Lescure is now fighting to preserve what parliament, debt markets and the next election have not yet dismantled.

France’s public debt is projected to exceed 120% of GDP in 2027. Investors now demand more interest to lend to Paris than to Rome. 

On October 1, France’s 10-year borrowing spread over Germany reached 149 basis points, its widest level since 2012. 

Macron began with labor-market changes, corporate-tax cuts and the PACTE law, a package meant to make French business more competitive. 

Then the Yellow Vest protests erupted in 2018 after a carbon-tax increase on fuel. The government backed down and spent more than €10 billion on tax breaks and bonuses for lower-income workers. Macron’s reform project found its electoral limit at the petrol station.

Covid completed the conversion. 

France spent around €190 billion on Covid-related crisis and stimulus policies from 2020 through 2022, then roughly €72 billion during the energy crisis that followed Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. 

Macron built his reputation on fiscal modernization and kept it alive through emergency spending.

France still has achievements to show for it. Employment is higher, the labor market functions better, and France’s growth over the decade was beaten among Europe’s major economies only by Spain. 

The bill has arrived anyway. Lescure’s budget plan combines spending cuts, freezes on public-sector wages and some pensions, extended taxes on large companies and tighter tax exemptions. 

His minority government must negotiate every measure with a parliament built to block it.

The opposition is waiting with demolition permits. The National Rally has attacked Macron’s pension changes and favors retirement at 60. 

Jean-Luc Mélenchon wants higher taxes on companies and wealthy households, sharper wage increases, and a plan to cancel or freeze debt held by the central bank. France’s next election may decide which faction dismantles Macron’s project first.

Macron wanted France to anchor a Europe independent of America, Russia and China. He leaves a country where the treasury must reassure bond traders and the government cannot reliably pass a budget.

He built a start-up nation. The market has priced it as a distressed asset.

📄 Ghalibaf: Caucasus must not become arena for rivalry among foreign powers

📌 Tehran, IRNA - Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said the Caucasus region must not become an arena for geopolitical rivalry among foreign powers.

Speaking during a meeting with Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan on Monday, Ghalibaf referred to the current situation in the Persian Gulf and said experience had shown that interference by extra-regional powers could lead to insecurity.
​
Ghalibaf thanked the Armenian people and government for their positions and actions in support of Iran during the recent US-Israeli aggression. He said Iran’s “definite policy” was to develop and strengthen relations with neighboring countries at both operational and strategic levels, adding that Armenia was an important opportunity for expanding ties with Iran.
​
He also expressed hope that a strategic cooperation treaty between Iran and Armenia would be finalized soon.
​
Mirzoyan, for his part, said Armenia would not allow its territory to be used for actions against Iran.
​
He stressed that preserving the existing borders of countries in the region was very important to Armenia.
​
Mirzoyan described Armenia’s relations with Iran as strategic and called for expanded bilateral cooperation. He added that Armenia sought to develop its transportation links with neighboring countries.
